claims.claim: Barolo is 100% Nebbiolo.
Gianetto is an official Barolo MGA. It is on the disciplinare's list.
Gianetto is in the commune of Serralunga d'Alba.
Kermit Lynch describes a prime southeastern exposure to catch the morning sun.
claims.quote: prime southeastern exposure to catch the morning sun

claims.claim: Garesio's Gianetto parcel faces east. Their factsheet lists south, southeast and east.
claims.note: Another producer's parcel in the same MGA.

claims.claim: Serralunga is on Helvetian soil: Lequio formation of white clay with layers of limestone sand. Kermit Lynch lists clay and limestone.
claims.quote: Lequio formation with white clay interspersed with layers of limestone sand

claims.claim: The MGA is small. Garesio's Gianetto parcel is 0.6 ha; its factsheet says about 1 ha.
claims.note: Another producer's holding, not the MGA's total and not Porro's plot.

claims.claim: Kermit Lynch's 2015 sheet lists Porro's Gianetto vineyard as about 1 ha on clay and limestone. A separate listing says 2 ha with 40 to 45 year old vines.
claims.note: Vine age and size conflict across listings; second listing not clearly tied to Porro.

claims.claim: Altitude is about 250 to 280 m at Garesio's Gianetto parcel; one source says 280 to 350 m.
Vine age for Porro's Gianetto is uncertain: 40 to 45 years in one listing, 8 years in another.
The 2015 Gianetto was 14.5% alcohol.
Natural fermentation, aging in Slavonian oak botti, bottled unfiltered. Applies to the estate's Barolos.
claims.note: Kermit Lynch 4-pack page. Primal Wine confirms large oak botti, not the wood origin.

claims.claim: Wine Advocate: plump and ripe, with dark fruit and blackberry. Spice of crushed clove or powdered cinnamon, plus bay leaf, dried herb and lavender.
claims.quote: plump and ripe with dark fruit
claims.note: Wine.com shows Wine Advocate 92 points; the reviewer is not named on the page.

claims.claim: Kermit Lynch says the Gianetto is not the unyielding, tannic beast of old, and should still gain from a few years in the cellar.
claims.quote: will certainly benefit from a few years in your cellar
claims.note: Quote read for 2017 and repeated in 2018 summary.

claims.claim: No critic or producer window found for the 2018. Vinous gave the 2017 Gianetto 2024 to 2034.
Estimate: drink 2026 to 2036, best 2028 to 2034. Gianetto is a more approachable Serralunga Barolo. Fits the CellarTracker 2026 to 2034 range.
claims.note: Reasoned from the 2017 Vinous window, Kermit Lynch 'few years in the cellar' note and CellarTracker range.

claims.claim: Guido Porro is the fourth generation of the family, in Serralunga d'Alba. He took over from his father Giovanni in 1996.
claims.quote: fourth generation of the Porro family

claims.claim: The family has bottled under its own label since the late 1970s.
All of Guido's Barolos come from three MGAs in Serralunga: Lazzarito (Lazzairasco, Santa Caterina, 'l Pari), Gianetto and Vigna Rionda (a 0.7 ha plot).
claims.note: Vinexus says three MGAs; details on parcels vary by summary.

claims.claim: Lazzairasco is the lower site below the winery; Santa Caterina is higher up and more high-toned.
Taste dots: dry; full body (plump and ripe); fresh acidity; firm tannin, typical of Serralunga.
Flavor icons from the Wine Advocate note: blackberry, clove, bay leaf, lavender.
Braised beef, roast game, mushroom risotto and aged cheese suit Barolo.
Decant one to two hours while young.
